item.content:encoded:
I was going to recommend you reread it because you're pretty far off, but I think I actually have to knock myself here for not being as clear as I could have been. Addendum 10-16-1991 states "No male specimens of SCP-939 have yet been identified," and that means ever. As far as the Foundation is aware1, the 'species,' as it were, is entirely female. There are real-world corollaries to this in a number of reptiles and probably others besides. So no, as far as a male 939 goes, that was not a thing here. I should probably work the fact that 939 are, so far as the Foundation know, exclusively female into the Description.

Regarding the Silent Night
+ show block
– hide block

The matter of the "Silent Night" is, however, intended to be somewhat more ambiguous. I had on one of my sandboxes a tentative classification system for qualifying the severity of a containment breach, based on a number of factors including: whether contact with the facility was maintained or lost; whether anything was able to fully escape the facility; how much of what did escape the Foundation was able to subsequently recapture; whether the failure was severe enough to warrant the activation of facility failsafe measures2; whether failsafe measures did indeed activate; whether failsafe measures were effective; whether the facility is recoverable; and some other factors besides. A "Silent Night," then, is among the most dire scenarios. In short, it means the facility completely dropped out of contact with the outside world, SCPs breached containment and were unrecoverable, site failsafe measures should have activated but (to outside observers, apparently) failed to, the site is a total loss, survivors are not expected, and the likelihood of ever knowing what actually happened is slim. I never properly finished this classification system and so its presence and consistency on the wiki will be spotty - I know a couple people liked the idea and used it or something similar. The only contextual bit of evidence included here to guess at the severity of a "Silent Night" is the statement that nearby settlements are being evacuated and recovery crews dispatched - and, by the way, might I direct your attention to the date on SCP-938's attached photo?

I originally intended to do a piece about Bio-Containment and Research Site-06's Silent Night from the POV of someone there, but I ran out of steam. Couldn't get it to jive the way I wanted it to.

tl;dr No, there's nothing you really missed. Just a couple misinterpretations - partially my fault, a breach classification system I hinted at but never properly expounded upon, and some ancillary documents I never properly wrote. But you are intended to feel like something's been left out, because it has.

Footnotes
1. or at least, was aware as of that time
2. Which for a bioketer site is going to mean sterilization up to and potentially including detonation of on-site thermonuclear weapon(s)

item.content:encoded:
Not ears, but they do 'hear.' When I wrote this, my thinking was the dorsal ridge/spines functioned as ears/whiskers/something like antennae, detecting vibrations in the air/aberrations and changes in air flow. I don't think I did a very good job of conveying the breadth of their sensory capabilities; one of the main intended spook factors of these things is that you are just not hiding from them. They can feel heartbeats and every breath, let alone someone's actual movements.

I always intended to write a bit of errata, in the form of a mission briefing or orientation given to people who may soon be in direct or indirect contact with them, elaborating on these things. Was going to have a bit where the presenter says something with the general gist of, "Seeing these things, the grin of glowing red teeth in the dark, you might feel relieved if they turn away. You think it didn't notice you, that it's about to move on… Their sensory organs are primarily oriented laterally along their body. If they turn and expose their flank, they're presenting more of the pit organs that rim their jaws, and the dorsal ridge - plainly, they're looking straight at you, and they see you. Don't ever doubt that; always assume they know you're there, whether you see them or not, even if intel says they're confined to a sublevel, to the next building over… But the one to kill you is seldom the one you see. There's a reason the first resort of any MTF that has to deal with these things is to query the availability of better-suited AMTF units, and the second resort is to requisition enough VX to make the weapons and logistics folks spit-take. But don't misunderstand - the AMTFs bring it, too, and the armories typically serving them are a little more accustomed."

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The timeline's pretty accurate, though I won't confirm or refute any of the inferences, and it's correct that 914 was not involved in the vivisection of the specimen kept on ice.

+ show block
– hide block

There really are no hints as to what they are, or their origins. I didn't intend to provide any of those. The goal was to write these as things which simply are, with the in-universe backdrop of the Foundation coming to terms with that, and out-of-universe, leave the reader to do the same. That's my favorite sort of strangeness: the things that just are, without explanation or apology. For me, those things have the most fun implications for the world they exist in. Chiefly:

Job 38:4 - Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.

Or for those playing the home game, the idea that the Foundation, for all their esoteric measurements and self-assured authority, has no clue how the world works and what rules it follows, if there are any at all. The Lovecraftian idea of humanity residing on an island, and that they were never intended to wander far. That's the spirit I try to write in. One of the ways I try to do it is by giving the reader such facts as the Foundation would have to work with, while abstaining from any and all conjecture in-article. I can be fairly ham-fisted about it, I admit.

The questions I intended for this to leave were things like, "Why and how does the dismembered specimen in Cryo talk, and appear to refer to itself in plural? Does it know what it's saying? Why do they kill and feed when it not only serves no purpose, but eventually hinders them? What is 914 doing to them and why? How does anything kill them/what keeps them going?" etc. I wanted to give the broad-strokes silhouette of something which, in the face of our presumed understanding of the world, is fundamentally wrong and makes no real sense at all.

Though, as far as what they are goes, I've been asked if they were intended to be things from real-world mythologies, or the source of those myths in the Foundation-verse. Things like changelings, the ghuls(sp?) of Arabic myth, or the source of the African folktales of hyenas that would stand outside of huts at night, calling the names of people within, devouring them when they emerged to answer. I was inordinately pleased that they wound up seeming to align with so many such things. Lovecraft's "Pickman's Model" was a big part of my inspiration for them, and that's probably my favorite story of his, mostly for Pickman's "They knew how to live," rant.

Little bit drink and tired and pretty sure I'm babbling at this point so I'll shut up now. Glad you enjoyed it, though. Always nice to hear.


Please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

EDIT: Also, WRT the "date with the lady in red" thing, there was supposed to be pictures to go with it. Scans of the notebook the guy carried around with him, containing notes of his observations of 939 specimens. One of them being - well, I guess it requires some setup, but anyway - when the Foundation is trying to pull one out, they gas them all with powerful tranquilizers and go in kitted out in MOPP-4 ready to waste everything, grab one while it's sedated, get out, hit decon, etc. So one of the observations was, when the fans which would usually vent the tranquilizer into the room are turned on, some of them would drop to the ground motionless acting as if they were drugged, even when the Foundation wasn't actually pumping anything in. The guy would then wonder if it was Pavlovian conditioning of the 939 specimens, or attempted active deception on their part, or possibly something else entirely. And then over the top of all this guy's notes, he'd have written in red pen, "LADY IN RED; DON'T FORGET!" and things like that, over, and over, and over, on all of it. Ideally so the notes underneath were still at least partially legible.

item.title: Get out of there, phantom how.
item.content:encoded:
Glad you like it.

We spent about six months writing this, maybe eight, getting feedback the whole time. Wish I hadn't deleted my old sandbox, or I could tell you. Either way, this is what inclusive "we" does. Wouldn't be half so refined in delivery if I hadn't sought feedback as I wrote, and tuned accordingly, so that's my advice if you want it: listen to what people say, and if they simply instruct you that you should change it, don't. First, listen to the why, consider it, and then write it as seems best to you. I got a lot of tl;dr type sentiments writing this, and it wouldn't be what it is if I'd listened to those sentiments that questioned its merits on the basis of length. It's as long as it needs to be to do what was intended, and I'm glad to hear that's appreciated.

Plus, the fact that it was written so slowly meant there was a lot of time to reflect on what else could be done, or what could be done better, before anyone felt like anything was set. Probably most proud of this, out of what I've written so far.

My favorite part was the 914 test, I think. That was a total afterthought, but also seemed to be the most chilling insight. That was also questioned on its merits, for being a cross-test rather than length, but still.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Safe/Elucid/Keter isn't about danger per se, it's about difficulty of containment and the threat to the "masquerade" that a given SCP represents if containment fails.

An antimatter bomb capable of destroying the planet would be Safe if it could be put in a crate and never touched again without consequence.

A hamster that turned invisible for 15 seconds every second tuesday would be Elucid because it requires upkeep. The fact that it's almost entirely harmless means nothing. Its cage needs to be cleaned, it needs food and water, it can't be shoved in the back of a locker and forgotten about until the heat death of the universe.

These creatures require special accommodations to maintain, special training/procedures to guard against escape, represent a significant exposure risk if they get out and are not, to the best of our knowledge, self-limiting. We don't know for sure that they won't eat the entire planet if they get the chance. Plus, there may be more of these things in the wild, we just don't know. That means Keter.

:edit:

Added "Plus, there…know."

item.content:encoded:
Litfried:

The "pointless ickyness" isn't pointless. It's part of the article's intended fridge horror, but it doesn't work for everyone. I erred on the side of understatement with it.

Veldi:

An argument could be made for 966 being Keter, being that they're difficult to track, actively hostile, and simple proximity is enough to cause irreversible injury. However, this is also mitigated by the fact that they're exceedingly frail, do not primarily prey on humans, and tend to travel in smaller numbers.

939 are also hard to track, hostile, and unprotected proximity can be harmful due to amnestic exposure, assuming one makes it out alive. 939 are much harder to kill due to the non-reliance on/total lack of certain organ systems, tendency to be encountered in larger numbers, and specialization for preying specifically on humans. 939 also pose a greater risk to the Foundation's goal of secrecy because of their methods of reproduction.
